chunks: Al-Hakim Abu Ali Al-Husayn ibn Ahmad al-Bayhaqi narrated to us, saying: He narrated to me Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Sawli, saying: He narrated to me Abu Abdullah Muhammad ibn Musa ibn Nasr al-Razi, saying: I heard my father saying:

A man said to Ar-Ridha (peace be upon him): 'By God, there is no one on the face of the Earth whose fathers are nobler than yours.' He replied: 'Piety granted them nobility, and obedience to God enabled them to benefit from it.'
Another man said to him: 'By God, you are the best of the people.' He said to him: 'Do not swear, O this man. Better than me is he who is more God-conscious and more obedient to Him.'
By God, no verse has abrogated this verse: 'And We made you into nations and tribes, that you may know each other. Verily, the most honored of you in the sight of God is the most righteous of you.'

key_terms.لِتَعَارَفُوا: That you may know each other

ai.seo_question: What is the basis of true nobility according to Imam Ar-Ridha (a.s.)?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida*, Imam Ar-Ridha (a.s.) refutes the Abbasid-era claim of superiority based on lineage by elevating *Taqwa* (piety) as the true metric of nobility, directly countering the political ideology of his time. He explicitly cites Surah Al-Hujurat, verse 13, noting its continued validity (*nasakh*) to affirm that divine honor is granted to the most righteous, thereby establishing a theological basis for the Shi'a understanding of merit over mere ancestry.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 58-10 Al-Hakim Abu Ali Al-Husayn ibn Ahmad al-Bayhaqi narrated that Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Sowli quoted on the authority of Abu Abdullah Muhammad ibn Musa ibn Nasr al-Razi that he had heard his father say,

“A man told Ar-Ridha’ (a.s.), ’By God, considering who your father is, there is no one on the Earth who is nobler than you are.’ Ar-Ridha’ (a.s.) replied, ‘Piety granted them this nobility, and obedience to God enabled them to benefit from it.’
Someone else said, ‘By God, you are the best of the people.’ Then Ar-Ridha’ (a.s.) said, “Do not swear. Whoever fears God the Sublime more than me is better than I am, and is more obedient than I am.

By God, the following verse has not been abolished, ‘…and made you into nations and tribes, that ye may know each other (not that ye may despise (each other). Verily the most honored of you in the sight of God is (he who is) the most righteous of you…’”
